threads.thread_goal: Align on scope, success metrics, and initial call type mapping for the playbook.

messages.text: Hi team, welcome to the Omnichannel Customer Service Playbook project. We have 21 days to design and roll out a unified playbook covering phone, chat, and in-store interactions. The goal is to improve consistency and first-contact resolution across all channels. I'd like to start by mapping our top customer scenarios. Can everyone share the most common call types and in-store interaction patterns you see? We'll use this to prioritise what goes into the playbook first. Looking at T1 and A2, we need to identify the top 10 call types with volumes and pain points.

Thanks for kicking this off. From my experience on the contact centre side, I'd say the top call types are: billing inquiries, product information requests, order status checks, returns and refunds, and technical issues. We also get a fair number of complaints about delivery delays. I can start documenting these with rough volumes if that helps. Should I pull data from our current system or estimate based on what I see daily?

Good start. From the in-store side, I'd add: product recommendations, special orders, loyalty program questions, and cross-sell opportunities during checkout. The challenge is that our sellers often handle these differently depending on the store. We should also capture escalation patterns—when do customers ask to speak to a supervisor or request a callback?

From the bookshop perspective, I see distinct patterns: genre-based recommendations, special publication orders (which can take weeks), customer reading preference discovery, and handling out-of-stock situations. These are quite different from general retail, so we'll need tailored guidance. I can draft a quick summary of the top 5 bookshop scenarios by end of day if that's useful.
I think we should focus on the contact centre call types first. The in-store stuff can come later. Let me know what data you need and I'll try to pull it. Not sure how long it will take though.

Actually, we need both in parallel. The playbook is omnichannel, so we can't separate them. Let me clarify: we're looking for the top 10 combined scenarios across all channels. 7284, can you pull actual call volumes from the system for the types you mentioned? 52506, can you document the in-store patterns with frequency estimates? 125944, your bookshop summary would be really helpful. Let's aim to have this consolidated by tomorrow EOD so we can move to the next step.

I can pull the call data by tomorrow morning. I'll need to check with the reporting team to make sure I'm using the right metrics, but I should have volumes and basic pain points documented. Will that work?

I'll compile the in-store patterns. I've been tracking some of this informally, so I can pull together a quick summary. One thing though—should we also include the escalation paths in this mapping, or is that a separate exercise?

Good question. Let's include escalation paths in the mapping. That's part of T1 anyway. So for each call type, note when and why it gets escalated. This will feed into the quality monitoring and coaching framework later.

I'll have the bookshop summary ready by EOD tomorrow. I'm also thinking about the success metrics—for bookshop, we should track recommendation acceptance rate and special order fulfillment time. Should I include those in my summary or wait for a separate metrics discussion?

Include them in your summary. We'll be defining success metrics as part of T12, so having channel-specific ideas now will help. Speaking of which, let me share what I'm thinking for baseline metrics: first-contact resolution rate, customer satisfaction score, average handling time, and compliance adherence. We'll need to confirm these with stakeholders and identify data sources. Does everyone have access to current reporting tools to pull this data?
I can access the contact centre reporting dashboard. Not sure about in-store data though. 52506, do you have access to store-level metrics?

We have some store dashboards, but they're not as detailed as the contact centre ones. I can pull satisfaction scores and transaction data, but first-contact resolution is harder to track in-store. We might need to define that differently for in-store interactions—maybe 'issue resolved without escalation' or something similar.

That's a good point. We'll need to adapt metrics by channel. Let's capture that in T12. For now, let's focus on getting the call type mapping and initial metrics framework done. Once we have the top 10 scenarios and baseline data sources confirmed, we can move forward with drafting scripts and guidelines. I'll consolidate everything you send me tomorrow and we'll review it as a group.
Sounds good. Let me know if you need anything from my end. I'm still getting up to speed on the project, so I might have questions as we go.

I'll have everything ready by tomorrow morning. One more thing—should the playbook include specific language for handling sensitive topics like returns or complaints? I'm thinking about tone and empathy guidelines.

Absolutely. That's part of the standard scripts we'll draft in T2. We'll include opening, verification, and closing scripts with guidance on tone and empathy. That's a separate thread, but good to keep in mind. Alright, let's reconvene tomorrow with the data. I'll send a summary of what we've discussed and what we're waiting for.

Quick recap from our kickoff discussion: we've identified preliminary call types and in-store scenarios. 7284 is pulling contact centre call volumes, 52506 is documenting in-store patterns, and 125944 is preparing bookshop-specific scenarios. We're also discussing baseline metrics: first-contact resolution, customer satisfaction, handling time, and compliance adherence. Data sources will vary by channel. Next step: consolidate the top 10 scenarios and confirm success metrics. This feeds into A2 and T12. We'll review consolidated data tomorrow and make a final decision on which scenarios to prioritise.
Got it. I'll have the call volume data ready by 10am tomorrow. Should I format it in a specific way or just send a summary?
Send it as a simple table with call type, volume, and top 2-3 pain points. I'll consolidate everything into A2 format. Thanks.
I'll do the same for in-store. Should I include escalation frequency in the pain points section?
Yes, include escalation frequency. That's critical for T1. Once I have all three inputs, I'll create a consolidated A2 and we'll review it together to confirm D1—the final list of top 10 scenarios.
Perfect. I'll follow the same format for bookshop scenarios. See you all tomorrow.

Great. One final note: once we confirm the top 10 scenarios and baseline metrics, we'll have locked in D1 and D2. That clears the path for the next threads on scripts, guidelines, and the full playbook. Looking forward to seeing what you all bring tomorrow.

threads.thread_goal: Draft and iterate on standard call handling and quality monitoring approach.

messages.text: Now that we have the top 10 scenarios locked in, let's move to drafting standard scripts and quality monitoring. I've prepared a first draft of call opening, verification, and closing scripts based on best practices and our current approach. I'm also sharing an initial quality monitoring scorecard. Please review both and share feedback. We need to iterate quickly so we can get these approved by end of week. The scripts will feed into A1 and A6, and the scorecard into A3. T2 and T3 are the main tasks here.

I've reviewed the opening script draft. It looks solid overall. One thing I noticed—the verification section asks for too much information upfront. Customers get frustrated when we ask for account number, email, and phone all at once. Maybe we could ask for one identifier first, then verify the rest as we go? I can suggest some tweaks if you want.

Good catch. That's exactly the kind of feedback we need. Yes, please share your suggested tweaks. The goal is to make it practical for agents to use without slowing down the call. What's your experience with the current verification flow?

Currently, we ask for the order number first if it's an order-related call, or email if it's account-related. That usually gets us 80% of the way there. Then we ask for verification only if needed. I'll draft a revised version and post it by tomorrow morning.

I looked at the scripts too. For in-store, the opening and closing are fine, but the verification section doesn't really apply the same way. In-store, we're usually face-to-face, so verification is different. Should we have separate scripts for in-store, or adapt the contact centre version?

Good question. The scripts should be adaptable by channel. The core structure stays the same, but the verification and closing can differ. For in-store, verification might be 'Can I get your name and phone number for the order?' instead of account verification. Let's note that in the final version. 52506, can you draft in-store adaptations for the opening and closing?
Sure, I can do that. I'll also check with 125944 on bookshop-specific language. Some of our greeting and closing language might be different for bookshop customers.

Yes, bookshop interactions are quite different. The opening should acknowledge the customer's reading interests or current browsing. The closing should include information about special order timelines and follow-up. I'll draft bookshop-specific versions and send them over by tomorrow. I can also suggest some language for handling sensitive situations like out-of-stock items.

Perfect. So we'll have contact centre, in-store, and bookshop versions of the core scripts. That's exactly what we need for an omnichannel playbook. Now, let's talk about the quality monitoring scorecard. 291562, I'd like your input on the scoring rubric. What criteria do you think are most important for evaluating call quality?
Um, I think the main things are whether the agent solved the problem and if they were polite. Maybe also if they followed the script. I'm not sure what else would matter.

Those are good starting points. Let me expand: resolution, politeness, script adherence, compliance (data privacy, legal requirements), and efficiency (handling time). The scorecard should have clear criteria for each, with examples of good and bad behaviours. That's part of T3. I've drafted a rubric, but I want to make sure it's practical for supervisors to use. Can you review it and let me know if it's clear?
I'll take a look. Not sure how long it will take me to review, but I'll get to it when I can.
I can also review the scorecard from an agent perspective. I know what makes sense to track and what feels like micromanagement. Happy to give feedback.

Great. That's really helpful. Agent perspective is crucial. 7284, can you review by EOD tomorrow? And 291562, whenever you get to it. We also need to think about quick-reference checklists for agents and sellers. That's T8. These should be one-page reminders of key steps. 7284, since you're drafting the scripts, can you also draft the agent checklist?

Sure, I can draft the agent checklist. I'll base it on the opening, verification, and closing scripts, plus the scorecard criteria. Should it include things like 'confirm customer contact info' and 'document issue in system'?

Yes, exactly. The checklist should cover the full call flow: greeting, verification, issue handling, resolution, and closing. Include system documentation and compliance checks. Keep it to one page. 52506, can you draft a similar checklist for in-store interactions?

I'll draft the in-store checklist. It'll be a bit different since we don't have phone verification, but the flow is similar. I'll include things like greeting, understanding customer needs, product recommendations, and closing with next steps.

Perfect. So we have: 7284 revising the verification script and drafting the agent checklist, 52506 drafting in-store script adaptations and in-store checklist, 125944 drafting bookshop script adaptations, and 291562 reviewing the scorecard rubric. I'll consolidate everything by end of week and we'll do a final review. The goal is to have D3 and D4 locked in by Friday so we can move to the in-store and bookshop guidelines thread.

I'll have the bookshop scripts ready by tomorrow EOD. I'm also thinking about adding some guidance on handling difficult customers—like when someone is upset about a special order delay. Should that be in the scripts or in a separate section?

Good thinking. That can be in the scripts as part of the closing section, or as a separate 'handling difficult situations' section in A1. We'll decide once we see the draft. For now, include it in your bookshop script adaptations and we'll refine it during consolidation.
One more thing—should the scripts include language for offering escalation or callback options? I know some customers prefer to be called back rather than wait on hold.

Absolutely. That's part of the closing script. We should offer callback or escalation as options when appropriate. I'll make sure that's in the draft. Alright, let's reconvene with drafts by EOD tomorrow. We'll review and iterate, then aim for final approval by Friday.

Summary of TH2 progress: we're drafting standard call scripts (opening, verification, closing) with channel-specific adaptations for contact centre, in-store, and bookshop. 7284 is revising verification and drafting agent checklist. 52506 is adapting scripts for in-store and drafting in-store checklist. 125944 is drafting bookshop-specific scripts. We're also iterating on the quality monitoring scorecard (A3, T3) with input from 291562 and 7284. Quick-reference checklists (T8, A6) are being drafted in parallel. Target: lock in D3 (scripts) and D4 (scorecard) by Friday EOD.
Got it. I'll have the revised verification script and agent checklist ready by tomorrow morning. Looking forward to seeing everyone's drafts.
I'll have the in-store adaptations and checklist ready by tomorrow as well. This is coming together nicely.

Bookshop scripts will be ready by tomorrow EOD. I'm also preparing some examples of good and bad recommendation dialogues to include in the final playbook. Should those go in A1 or in a separate section?
Include them in your draft and we'll decide during consolidation. They could go in A1 as examples or in a separate guidelines section. We'll see what makes sense once we have everything together.

threads.thread_goal: Define in-store specialised seller and bookshop-specific guidelines.

messages.text: Now that we have the core scripts and quality monitoring framework, let's focus on in-store and bookshop-specific guidelines. I've drafted initial sales and cross-sell scripts for specialised sellers based on common scenarios from our top 10 list. These cover product recommendations, upselling, and handling customer objections. I'm sharing this for review and feedback. The goal is to balance solving customer issues with relevant product suggestions. This feeds into A5 and T4.

I've reviewed your draft. It's solid, but I think the cross-sell prompts might be too aggressive for some scenarios. For example, when a customer is returning an item, jumping straight to 'Would you like to try our new product line?' feels off. Maybe we should have different cross-sell strategies depending on the situation—more subtle for complaints, more direct for satisfied customers?

That's a really good point. I didn't think about the context that much. You're right—the tone should shift based on whether the customer is happy or frustrated. Let me revise the scripts to include context-specific guidance. I can add notes like 'If customer is satisfied, offer cross-sell. If customer is frustrated, focus on resolution first.'

Excellent. That's exactly the kind of nuance we need. 52506, can you revise the scripts with context-specific guidance by tomorrow? And 125944, I know you're working on the bookshop guidelines. Can you share your draft so we can review both in parallel?

I'm finalising the bookshop guidelines now. I've drafted a checklist for understanding customer reading preferences, a process for handling special publication orders, and examples of recommendation dialogues. The key difference from general retail is that bookshop recommendations are more consultative—we're helping customers discover books, not just selling. I'll share the draft by EOD today.

Perfect. That's the right approach. Bookshop is consultative, retail is transactional with cross-sell. Both are valuable, just different. Once you share the draft, I'll review both A5 and A4 together to make sure they're consistent in tone and approach.

I'm curious about the bookshop guidelines. Are they going to be separate from the main playbook, or integrated? And how do they connect to the contact centre side? Do we need to train contact centre agents on bookshop recommendations too?

Good question. The bookshop guidelines will be a separate section in the playbook, but the core principles (listening, understanding customer needs, making relevant suggestions) are the same. Contact centre agents don't need to be bookshop experts, but they should understand the process for special orders and know when to escalate to a bookshop specialist. I'll include a section on that in the guidelines.

That makes sense. So the playbook will have: core omnichannel principles, contact centre scripts and quality monitoring, in-store sales and cross-sell scripts, and bookshop-specific guidelines. All connected by the same service philosophy. That's A1, A3, A4, A5, and A6. Once we have all the drafts, we'll consolidate into the main playbook. Let's aim to have D5 and D6 locked in by end of week.

I'll have the revised in-store scripts with context-specific guidance ready by tomorrow. I'm also thinking about adding a section on handling product knowledge gaps—what to do when a seller doesn't know the answer to a customer question. Should that be in the scripts or in a separate coaching section?

That's a good addition. Include it in the scripts as a 'what to do if you don't know' section. Something like 'If you don't know the answer, offer to find out and follow up within 24 hours.' That's part of the service standard. We can also reference it in the quality monitoring scorecard.

I'm including something similar in the bookshop guidelines. For bookshop, it's important to acknowledge when you don't know a book or author, but offer to research or connect the customer with a colleague who might know. It's about maintaining credibility while being helpful.

Exactly. That's the right tone. Alright, let's consolidate by end of week. 52506, revised in-store scripts by tomorrow. 125944, bookshop guidelines by EOD today. I'll review both and we'll do a final check for consistency and tone. Then we'll move to the main playbook consolidation thread.
Got it. I'll have the revised scripts ready by tomorrow morning. One more thing—should we include pricing guidance in the cross-sell scripts, or is that handled separately?

Good question. Pricing should be available in the system, so sellers can reference it, but the scripts should focus on value and benefits, not price. The scripts can say 'This product is available at [price]' but shouldn't lead with price. That's a sales principle. Include that guidance in the scripts.

For bookshop, pricing is less of a factor since books have fixed prices. But I'll include guidance on how to discuss price for special orders, which can vary based on availability and import costs. I'll have that in the guidelines.

Perfect. Alright, let's wrap up this thread. Summary: 52506 is revising in-store sales and cross-sell scripts with context-specific guidance by tomorrow. 125944 is finalising bookshop recommendation and special order guidelines by EOD today. Both will include guidance on handling knowledge gaps and pricing. We'll review for consistency and tone, then lock in D5 and D6 by end of week.
I'll send the bookshop guidelines by 5pm today. Looking forward to seeing the in-store scripts tomorrow.
Will do. I'll send the revised scripts by 10am tomorrow.

threads.thread_goal: Consolidate the omnichannel playbook and align on shared principles.

messages.text: We're now at the consolidation stage. I've compiled all the scripts, guidelines, and quality monitoring frameworks into a draft table of contents for the omnichannel playbook. The structure is: 1) Omnichannel service principles, 2) Contact centre call handling, 3) In-store specialised seller guidance, 4) Bookshop-specific guidelines, 5) Quality monitoring and coaching, 6) Quick-reference checklists. Before we finalise, I want to check for gaps, overlaps, and consistency. Please review the TOC and let me know if anything is missing or needs adjustment. This feeds into A1, T6, and T7.

I've reviewed the TOC. It looks comprehensive. One thing I'd suggest: add a section on 'Handling Difficult Situations' that applies across all channels. Things like angry customers, escalations, and when to involve a supervisor. Right now, that guidance is scattered across different sections.

That's a great suggestion. A dedicated section on difficult situations would improve clarity. I'll add that as section 2.5, between call handling and in-store guidance. It'll reference the quality monitoring criteria and escalation rules. Good catch.

I reviewed the TOC too. I think we should also add a section on 'Omnichannel Service Principles' at the very beginning—something that ties everything together and explains why we're doing this. Right now, the playbook jumps straight into contact centre procedures. A brief intro on shared principles would help sellers and agents understand the 'why' behind the scripts.

Absolutely. That's part of T6—aligning on shared service principles. I was planning to draft those, but I'd like input from everyone. What do you think the core omnichannel principles should be? Things like 'consistency across channels', 'customer-first approach', 'first-contact resolution'?

From an agent perspective, I'd add 'empathy' and 'clear communication'. Customers want to feel heard, not just processed. And they want to understand what's happening with their issue. Those are things that matter to me when I'm on a call.

I'd add 'consistency' and 'accountability'. Customers should get the same level of service whether they call, chat, or visit a store. And we should take responsibility for resolving issues, not just passing them along.

For bookshop, I'd emphasise 'expertise' and 'personalisation'. We're not just selling books; we're helping customers find the right book for them. That requires knowing our products and tailoring recommendations. I'd also add 'respect for customer time'—whether it's a quick question or a long consultation, we should be efficient and respectful.

These are all excellent. Let me synthesise: 1) Consistency across channels, 2) Customer-first approach, 3) First-contact resolution, 4) Empathy and clear communication, 5) Accountability, 6) Expertise and personalisation, 7) Respect for customer time. I'll draft a brief statement for each principle and we'll review. This is D7—the final set of omnichannel service principles.
Those principles sound good. I'm not sure I have much to add, but they make sense to me.

Thanks. Alright, I'll draft the principles and the updated TOC with the difficult situations section. I'll also need to review the playbook for compliance—making sure all scripts and procedures align with legal and data privacy requirements. That's T11. I'll flag any issues and we'll address them before final sign-off.

Should we also include a section on data privacy in the playbook? Like, what information we can ask for and how to handle customer data? I know we have compliance rules, but agents might not know them.

Good point. I'll include a brief data privacy section in the playbook—what information to ask for, how to handle it, and when to escalate. That's part of T11. We'll make sure it's clear and practical for agents and sellers.
I'll also review the in-store scripts for compliance. Some of our current practices might not align with data privacy rules. I'll flag anything I find.

Great. So the plan is: I'll draft the omnichannel principles and updated TOC by tomorrow. I'll also do a compliance review of all scripts and procedures. 52506, can you review the in-store scripts for compliance issues? 7284, can you review the contact centre scripts? We'll consolidate any flags and address them before final sign-off. Target: D8 (playbook v1.0 sign-off) by end of week.
I can review the contact centre scripts for compliance. I'll check for data privacy issues, legal language, and anything that might cause problems. I'll have feedback by tomorrow EOD.
I'll review the in-store scripts by tomorrow as well. I'll check for compliance and also make sure the language is practical for sellers to use.
I'll review the bookshop guidelines for compliance too. I want to make sure our special order process and customer data handling align with legal requirements.

Perfect. So we have a full compliance review happening in parallel. I'll consolidate all feedback and create a final version of A1 with all corrections. Once we have that, we'll do a final stakeholder review and lock in D8. Then we move to the pilot planning thread.

Summary of TH4: we've consolidated the omnichannel playbook structure and identified key gaps. 125944 suggested adding a 'Handling Difficult Situations' section. 52506 suggested adding 'Omnichannel Service Principles' at the beginning. We've drafted 7 core principles: consistency, customer-first, first-contact resolution, empathy, accountability, expertise, and respect for time. Compliance review is underway: 7284 reviewing contact centre scripts, 52506 reviewing in-store scripts, 125944 reviewing bookshop guidelines. I'm drafting the principles and updated TOC with a data privacy section. Target: D7 (principles) and D8 (playbook v1.0 sign-off) by end of week.

threads.thread_goal: Plan pilot training, collect feedback, and define next iteration.

messages.text: We're now ready to move into the pilot phase. The playbook v1.0 is finalised and approved. Now we need to plan the pilot training, collect feedback from teams, and identify improvements for v1.1. I'm proposing a 2-week pilot with 2-3 contact centre teams and 2-3 in-store locations, including at least one bookshop. We'll run training sessions and then collect feedback through a structured form. This is T9 and T10. Let me share the proposed pilot scope and training plan. Who's interested in volunteering to help with training delivery?

I'm interested in helping with the bookshop training. I can deliver the bookshop-specific session and also help with the general omnichannel principles. I know the bookshop teams well, so I can also help with feedback collection.
I can help with the in-store training. I'll deliver the in-store sales and cross-sell session. I can also help coordinate with the store managers to schedule the training.
I can help with the contact centre training. I can deliver the call handling and quality monitoring session. I'm also happy to help with feedback collection from agents.

Excellent. So we have: 7284 leading contact centre training, 52506 leading in-store training, 125944 leading bookshop training. I'll deliver the omnichannel principles and quality monitoring overview. 291562, can you help coordinate the logistics—scheduling, materials, attendance tracking?
Um, I can try. I'm not sure how much I can do, but I'll help with scheduling and materials if you tell me what to do.

Thanks. I'll send you a checklist of what needs to be done. For now, let's focus on the pilot scope and training dates. I'm proposing: Week 1 (next week) for contact centre training, Week 2 for in-store and bookshop training. That gives us 2 weeks of feedback collection before we consolidate and plan v1.1. Does that timeline work for everyone?

That timeline works for me. I'll need to coordinate with store managers, but I think we can get 2-3 stores ready by Week 2. Should we include all store types (general retail and bookshop) or focus on one type first?

Let's include both. We need feedback from all channels to validate the omnichannel approach. So: 2 contact centre teams, 2 general retail stores, 1 bookshop. That's a good mix. 52506, can you identify which stores and get manager buy-in by tomorrow? 125944, can you confirm the bookshop location?
I'll confirm the bookshop location by tomorrow. I'm thinking of the downtown location—they have a strong team and are usually open to trying new things. I'll check with the manager.
I'll identify the stores and get manager buy-in by tomorrow. I'm thinking of the mall location and the downtown location for general retail. Both have good teams and should be receptive.

Perfect. So we'll have: 2 contact centre teams (TBD), mall store, downtown store, and downtown bookshop. That's D9—the pilot scope and participating teams. Now let's talk about feedback collection. I want to create a simple feedback form that captures: what worked, what didn't, what was confusing, and what needs to change. T10 is about collecting and summarising this feedback. 52506, can you draft a feedback form?
I can draft a feedback form. Should it be different for contact centre agents vs. in-store sellers, or the same for everyone?

Good question. I'd say: same core questions for everyone, but with channel-specific examples. So 'What was confusing?' might have different examples for contact centre vs. in-store. That way we can compare feedback across channels but also capture channel-specific issues.
Got it. I'll draft a form with core questions and channel-specific examples. I'll aim to have it ready by tomorrow so we can use it during the training sessions.
One thing to consider: some agents might not want to give negative feedback in front of their supervisor. Should the form be anonymous?

Excellent point. Yes, the form should be anonymous. We want honest feedback, not what people think we want to hear. 52506, make sure the form doesn't ask for names or identifying information. We'll track feedback by role and channel, but not by individual.

I also think we should do some informal conversations during the training. Not just the form, but also asking people directly: 'What do you think? Does this make sense?' That way we can catch issues in real-time and adjust.

Great idea. So we'll have both formal feedback (the form) and informal feedback (conversations during training). That gives us richer data. Alright, let's consolidate the pilot plan. We have: pilot scope (D9), training schedule, feedback form, and informal feedback collection. Once we have all the feedback, we'll consolidate it into A8 and identify improvements for v1.1. That's D10—which improvements go into v1.1.

Summary of TH5: we've planned the pilot phase. Pilot scope (D9): 2 contact centre teams, 2 general retail stores (mall and downtown), 1 bookshop (downtown). Training delivery: 7284 leading contact centre, 52506 leading in-store, 125944 leading bookshop, me leading omnichannel principles. 291562 coordinating logistics. Timeline: Week 1 contact centre training, Week 2 in-store and bookshop training. Feedback collection: 52506 drafting anonymous feedback form with core questions and channel-specific examples. We'll also do informal feedback during training. Once we consolidate feedback into A8, we'll identify improvements for v1.1 (D10). This feeds into T9, T10, and T12.
I'm ready to start the contact centre training next week. I'll prepare some examples and scenarios to make it practical. Should I also prepare some role-play exercises?
Yes, role-play exercises would be great. That helps people practice the scripts in a safe environment. Keep them short and practical. I'll send you the training materials and agenda by tomorrow.
I'll also prepare some scenarios for the in-store training. I'm thinking of common customer situations and how to apply the scripts. Should I include some challenging scenarios, like angry customers?

Absolutely. Include some challenging scenarios. That's where the playbook really helps—when things get difficult. I'll send you the training materials by tomorrow. Alright, let's execute the pilot and reconvene with feedback in 2 weeks.
I'm ready for the bookshop training. I'll prepare some book recommendation scenarios and special order examples. See you all in 2 weeks with feedback.
